## Highlights

TigerMarkView 0.12.1 keeps less about what you read, lets you decide whether
documents may load web images, and makes several open windows work together.
It is the first release since 0.10.0: 0.11.0, 0.11.1 and 0.12.0 were prepared
but never published, and everything they contained is here.

- **Remote images are now a setting.** **View > Rendering > Load Remote Images**
  is on by default, so documents show web images exactly as before. Turn it off
  and neither the viewer nor PDF export sends any request for an `http://` or
  `https://` image; local images and images embedded in the document still
  show. The setting is remembered and applies at once to every TigerMarkView
  window, including windows that were already open.
- **No browsing history on disk.** The WebView2 engine that shows documents and
  exports PDFs now runs InPrivate, so viewing a document no longer leaves a
  history of file names and times in the browser engine's folder. The history
  earlier versions kept there is deleted the first time 0.12.1 starts.
- **No sign-in to proxy servers.** Web images are fetched without offering your
  Windows account to anyone — the image's server or a proxy server. Behind a
  proxy that requires signing in, web images do not load.
- **Links do not open network shares.** Clicking a link to a Markdown file on a
  network share or mapped network drive no longer opens it, because Windows
  would sign in to that computer with your account; the status bar says why.
  Opening a document on a share yourself, with **File > Open**, from Open
  Recent, or by dropping it on the window's bars or an empty window, works as
  before.
- **Several windows, one set of settings.** Each window now saves only the
  setting you change in it. Clearing Open Recent in one window keeps it cleared
  when another window later changes its theme, editor or anything else; recent
  files opened in different windows are all kept; and each window has its own
  rendered page, so two windows reloading at once no longer interfere.
- **Clear Recent Files.** **File > Open Recent > Clear Recent Files** empties
  the Open Recent list at once and saves the empty list. Your documents and your
  other settings are not touched, and the session's navigation history is kept.
- **Uninstalling removes TigerMarkView's local data.** An explicit uninstall
  — from **Settings > Apps**, the uninstaller, or `winget uninstall` — removes
  `%LocalAppData%\TigerMarkView` (settings, the Open Recent list, browser engine
  data) and `%TEMP%\TigerMarkView` (generated pages) for the Windows account
  that runs it. Your Markdown documents and exported PDFs are never touched.
- **A privacy statement for each version.** It describes what TigerMarkView
  stores, how to clear it, what uninstalling removes, and every network request:
  web images in documents and how to turn them off, documents you open from a
  network share, and the installer's download of a missing Microsoft runtime.
  This release publishes it as its `PRIVACY.md` asset, which never changes, and
  installs the identical file in the **Docs** folder.

## Upgrading

- Upgrading keeps your settings and your Open Recent list: installing 0.12.1
  over 0.10.0, `winget upgrade`, and the first install over an Inno Setup
  installation of 0.9.0 or earlier all preserve them. Only an explicit
  uninstall removes them. Remote images stay on unless you turn them off.
- TigerMarkView 0.10.0 and earlier left this data behind when uninstalled. If
  you uninstalled one of those versions, you can delete
  `%LocalAppData%\TigerMarkView` and `%TEMP%\TigerMarkView` yourself.

## Packaging and WinGet

- The installer is built with TigerSetup 0.14.0. Installation, the PATH option,
  Open with registration for `.md` and `.markdown`, and runtime installation
  behave as in 0.10.0.
- The WinGet manifests name this release's `PRIVACY.md` asset as the package's
  `PrivacyUrl`.
- Beside the installer, the release publishes `TigerMarkView-0.12.1-WinGet.zip`,
  the exact WinGet manifests submitted for this version, and `PRIVACY.md`.
  `SHA256SUMS.txt` and `release-artifacts.json` record the hashes of all three.

## Prerequisites and known limitations

- Windows 10 version 1809 or later, or Windows 11, x64.
- .NET Desktop Runtime 10 and the Microsoft Edge WebView2 Runtime. They are not
  bundled; the installer checks for both and installs a missing one from the
  download the WinGet catalog lists for it.
- This build is unsigned. Windows SmartScreen may warn on first run; the
  published `SHA256SUMS.txt` lets you confirm the download.
- `tiger-mark` has no settings and always loads the web images of the document
  it converts.
- A window picks up another window's theme, editor or other preference the
  next time it starts; Open Recent and Load Remote Images are shared at once.
- Uninstalling an all-users installation removes the data of the account that
  runs the uninstall. Other accounts keep their own folders.

## Install

- Download and run `TigerMarkView-0.12.1-win-x64-setup.exe` from the assets
  below. Per-user installation is the default and needs no elevation.
- `winget install ItTiger.TigerMarkView` once the package is accepted in the
  WinGet community repository.

## Privacy

TigerMarkView keeps its settings and the Open Recent list on your computer and
sends them nowhere. What it stores, how to clear it, what uninstalling removes,
and when it makes network requests are described in the
[privacy statement for this release](https://github.com/rkozlowski/TigerMarkView/releases/download/v0.12.1/PRIVACY.md).
